A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ControlSpeech. Their text, equations, figures, seven result tables, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original evaluations on VccmDataset test sets A–D, codec and SMSD ablations, mixture-count and noise-mode experiments, and distribution visualizations.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the out-of-domain evaluation and supplementary ablations in its appendices.

M1.justification: FACodec disentanglement, parallel masked codec generation, BERT-based SMSD, Gaussian mixtures, noise perturbation, and training/inference procedures are retained. The abbreviated main-text loss presentation does not change the method.

E1.justification: Both use the same VccmDataset coverage: in-domain style control, unseen-speaker cloning, unseen style descriptions, and many-to-many style control. The out-of-domain style evaluation moves to Appendix G without changing coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain Salle, PromptStyle, InstructTTS, and PromptTTS 2 for style control; VALL-E and MobileSpeech for cloning; and PromptStyle and InstructTTS for many-to-many control. GT Codec and ablated ControlSpeech rows also match.

E3.justification: Retained settings match, including test-set sizes of 1,500, 1,086, and 100 for A–C, metrics, training configuration, and MOS evaluation using 30 samples with at least 10 listeners each. Omitted disclosures and newly explicit ablation-encoder freezing do not establish a revised experiment.

E4.justification: Both retain codec-decoupling and SMSD ablations, the 3/5/7 mixture-count sweep, four noise modes, out-of-domain style testing, and the same t-SNE analysis. Relocation and shortened descriptions introduce no new analytical evidence.

E5.justification: MOS uncertainty reporting is unchanged; Table 1 identifies ± as standard deviation in both versions. Neither introduces additional run or seed information, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: All seven matched tables have identical entries and rankings. v2 Tables 3, 4, and 5 become v3 Tables 5, 3, and 4 respectively. Figure 3 retains the same distributions; no new empirical outcomes are reported.

T1.justification: Mathematical definitions and derivations are retained. The complete SMSD loss derivation in v2 Appendix C, Equation 10, matches v3 Appendix K, Equation 8. Main-text equations are shortened or presented inline without substantive mathematical revision.

C1.justification: v3 drops ControlToolkit as an explicit contribution and emphasizes VccmDataset instead. The central claims about independent speaker cloning and style control, SMSD novelty, and competitive performance remain. Adding 'Independent' to the title restates an existing claim.

C2.justification: v3 removes the attribution of GT Codec's emotion/speed limitations to accumulated evaluator errors and the discussion explaining why excluding neutral emotion makes evaluation harder. Interpretations concerning pitch-control difficulty, SMSD, and generalization remain; limitations and ethics are relocated.

D1.justification: v3 removes ControlToolkit's detailed resource inventory, source-dataset size figures, the GT Codec definition, neutral-emotion exclusion, and explicit VALL-E/MobileSpeech retraining disclosure. It newly specifies a frozen Encodec encoder in the decoupling ablation. Most architecture/training details and the code URL remain; actual resource withdrawal is not established.

R1.justification: v3 adds an explicit distinction concerning NaturalSpeech 3 generating its codec targets from the same textual content. It removes background citations including the GPT-4 technical report, FastDiff, and HiFi-GAN. Most research positioning, including the PromptTTS 2 distinction, is retained across relocation.

P1.justification: The abstract and contribution list are condensed and rewritten. Substantial related-work discussion and limitations move into the main text, while out-of-domain evaluation and ethics move into appendices. Appendix ordering and mathematical presentation are reorganized; title, author information, and acknowledgments also change.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout, substantially resizing and repositioning figures and tables. Figure 1 is restyled and relabeled; Figures 1 and 3 and several tables become much smaller. The out-of-domain results table moves into Appendix G.

improvement.justification: v3 makes related work and limitations more prominent and clarifies the NaturalSpeech 3 distinction. However, it removes useful evaluation context, including GT Codec's definition, neutral-emotion exclusion, and explicit cloning-baseline retraining, while retaining identical results. Reduced resource documentation and substantially smaller tables further weaken transparency and readability. These limited losses outweigh the organizational gains.
